elements.label: Figure 3.9
elements.description: Two small-area choropleth maps of poverty rates (2019) shown as regional zoom-ins. Left panel titled "Midlands & Northern Mountains": districts are shaded in a blue-to-orange diverging gradient; orange/dark orange districts (higher poverty) dominate the northwestern and northern parts and scattered areas along the western edge, while blue districts (lower poverty) cluster in the central-eastern and southeastern parts, especially along the eastern and southeastern edges and the central-south corridor. Right panel titled "Central Highlands": orange and light orange districts (higher poverty) cover most of the western and central parts, with darker orange in some northwest and central districts; blue districts (lower poverty) concentrate along the eastern edge and southeastern coast. Legend below both panels: a color bar labelled "Poverty rate" running from 0.0 (blue) through light neutral tones to 100.0 (dark orange/brown). Note: the color gradient transitions between blue and orange depicts the national average poverty rate from the 2019 small area poverty map; rates are higher in orange districts than the national average and lower in blue districts. Source: World Bank staff calculations.
